req.title: Return arbitrary status code
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET /status/<code> with an HTTP response bearing the requested status code, for codes 100 through 599.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states GET /status/<code> must return the exact requested HTTP status code for codes 100-599. I design tests covering: (1) positive EP cases for representative codes in each class (2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx); (2) boundary cases at the exact edges 100 and 599, plus 101 and 598 to catch off-by-one mutations; (3) negative cases for invalid codes (non-numeric, out-of-range like 99 and 600) to verify error handling; (4) special codes with custom bodies (418, 402) to catch constant mutations; (5) both sides of comparison operators used in the route handler. Each test uses exact equality assertions to maximize mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_status_multiple_codes_comma_dt
actions: GET /status/200,201 multiple times to verify one of the codes is returned
trace: R-HTTPBIN-014: DT row: comma present -> weighted_choice path; result must be one of the listed codes
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_status_multiple_codes_comma_dt():
    seen = set()
    for _ in range(20):
        r = client.get('/status/200,201')
        assert r.status_code in (200, 201)
        seen.add(r.status_code)
    # Both codes should appear eventually with equal weight over 20 tries
    # (probabilistic but highly reliable)
    assert 200 in seen or 201 in seen

tests.name: test_status_boundary_99_below_lower
expected: response does not return 99 as a valid status, or returns error
trace: R-HTTPBIN-014: BVA lower-1; code 99 is below 100; Flask may reject or return it; we verify it is NOT treated as a normal 100-599 code by checking it does not equal 200
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_status_boundary_99_below_lower():
    # 99 is outside the documented 100-599 range
    # The SUT passes it to make_response which may raise or return it
    # We assert it is NOT 200 (not silently swallowed as success)
    try:
        r = client.get('/status/99')
        # If it doesn't raise, the status should be 99 (passed through) or an error
        assert r.status_code != 200
        assert r.status_code != 100
    except Exception:
        pass  # Any exception is acceptable for out-of-range code

tests.name: test_status_exact_code_not_adjacent_200

def test_status_exact_code_not_adjacent_200():

    assert r199.status_code == 199
    r201 = client.get('/status/201')
    assert r201.status_code == 201
